_readme: Text for the Rules page. 'general' is our own short summary of the 2025 base game rulebook, which remains the authority. 'league' is a draft until the group votes on it.

general.intro: A quick refresher in our own words, based on the 2025 edition. If this page and your rulebook disagree, the rulebook wins.

sections.heading: The goal
items: Be the first to reach 10 victory points (VPs). You can only win on your own turn.
Settlements are worth 1 VP and cities are worth 2 VPs.
Longest Route and Largest Army are worth 2 VPs each, and each Victory Point card is worth 1 VP.

sections.heading: Your turn
items: You may play one development card before you roll.
Roll both dice. Every hex showing that number produces: 1 card per settlement and 2 per city on it. The hex holding the robber produces nothing.
Then trade, build and play a development card in any order, if you have not already played one this turn.
When you are done, pass the dice to your left.

sections.heading: Rolling a 7
items: Nobody collects resources.
Anyone holding more than 7 resource cards discards half of them, rounded down.
The roller moves the robber to a new hex and steals 1 random card from a player with a building on that hex.

sections.heading: Trading
items: On your turn you can trade with any player. Other players can only trade with you, not with each other.
With the supply you can trade 4 of one resource for 1 of another. A 3:1 port improves that to 3 of one resource, and a 2:1 port to 2 of the resource it shows.
You cannot give cards away, and that includes trading a resource for the same resource.

sections.heading: Building
items: Settlements must connect to one of your roads and sit at least two edges from every other building.
Cities replace one of your settlements.
Roads must connect to your own road or building, and cannot carry on through an opponent's building.
You have 15 roads, 5 settlements and 4 cities.

sections.heading: Development cards
items: The deck has 25 cards: 14 Knights, 5 Victory Points, 2 Road Building, 2 Year of Plenty and 2 Monopoly.
You can play only one per turn, and not on the turn you bought it.
Victory Point cards are the exception: you can reveal any number of them, even ones you just bought, if that wins you the game.

sections.heading: Longest Route and Largest Army
items: Longest Route goes to the first player with 5 continuous roads, and moves as soon as someone has more.
Largest Army goes to the first player to play 3 Knights, and moves as soon as someone has played more.

sections.heading: Playing with 3 or with 5–6
items: In a 3-player game, the white pieces are not used.

For 5–6 players you need the extension. In the 2025 edition each turn has a paired player: the third player to the left of the active player takes an Action phase straight after the active player, but cannot trade with other players.
Older editions of the extension use a special building phase instead, and older boxes call Longest Route 'Longest Road'.

league.status: Draft for the group to vote on
league.intro: These are a starting point, not a decree. Nothing here is final until the group has agreed it.

sections.heading: Who and what counts
items: Anyone can join: register yourself on the site, or ask someone at the table to do it. There is no fee and no try-out.
A league game has 3 to 6 registered players, all of whom agree before setup that it counts.
Agree the rules before the first settlement goes down: expansions, scenario, victory point target and any house rules.

sections.heading: Before the game
items: Roll for turn order, as the rulebook says.
Choose colours in turn order, unless the table agrees another way. Colours are logged, so superstitions can be tested.
Use the rules for the edition on the table. If people remember them differently, the rulebook decides.

sections.heading: When lunch runs out
items: If time runs out, finish the current round so everyone has had the same number of turns.
The player with the most VPs wins, counting any Victory Point cards they reveal. If tied, the tied player who would have had the next turn wins.
Log it with 'Ended early' ticked. It counts as a normal league game.

sections.heading: Logging results
items: Someone at the table logs the game the same day, with seats in turn order and everyone's final VPs. This needs a free GitHub account or the group password.
Everyone at the table should be happy with the entry. If you spot a mistake or something spurious, ask an admin to correct or remove it. All ratings then recalculate from scratch.
Abandoned games that nobody finished or time-called do not count.

sections.heading: Fair play
items: Trades happen immediately. Promises about future turns are welcome but cannot be enforced.
Answer honestly if someone asks how many resource cards you hold. Your cards and unplayed development cards stay hidden.
No playing to hand a win to a friend. Being a terrible negotiator is allowed, and indeed encouraged.

sections.heading: Scoring and variety
items: Every scoring system on the Scoring page runs side by side during the trial period. The group will then choose an official one and retire the rest.
Repeat match-ups count for less over time, so the league rewards playing against a wide range of people.
Players are marked provisional until they have played 5 games.

sections.heading: Leaving and returning
items: A retired player's history stays in the record, and they drop off the default leaderboard.
Anyone can come back at any time and carry on from their old rating.
